People fleeing the conflict in Sudan are trapped in a cycle of worsening food insecurity, repeated displacement and lost livelihoods, according to Noah Taylor, head of operations at the Norwegian Refugee Council. 

He says families are taking dangerous journeys across front lines and international borders in search of safety and stability. Around 13 million people are displaced outside Sudan, with many seeking refuge in neighbouring Chad and South Sudan. 

Taylor says humanitarian assistance remains drastically insufficient, with major gaps in shelter, education, healthcare and food supplies. 

Some families are selling their remaining assets or taking any available work simply to find enough food. 

He says families continue moving between displacement sites and across borders in search of stability and food assistance.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Trade talks meant to avert the latest 50 percent US tariffs on Canadian goods collapsed on Friday, tipping high-stakes negotiations into a full-blown trade war. Prime Minister Mark Carney told his negotiators to walk away, saying, "We were not prepared to compromise Canada's sovereignty or to undermine our key industries." 

Trump is using a 1930 law to sanction Canada over alleged discrimination against US businesses. Carney says Washington had demanded restrictions on Canada's ability to strike trade deals with other countries and sought changes to Canadian laws protecting the French language.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of people are fleeing violence in Sudan's Kordofan region, where the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are battling for control of a strategic supply route. More than 5,000 families arrived in El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, in a single week. As the army retakes some towns from the RSF, some are hopeful they could go home, while others fear what they'll find.

With millions already struggling to find enough food and poor rainfall threatening the harvest, the wait to return home is likely to grow harder. 

Al Jazeera's Almigdad Alruhaid reports.
